name: logtalk
why: A logic-programming language that fuses Prolog with object-oriented ideas, rarely encountered and genuinely odd to play with.

brief.what_it_is: Logtalk is a declarative object-oriented logic programming language that extends Prolog with modules, prototypes, classes, protocols (interfaces), and categories (components with hot patching). It is implemented as a transcompiler, so you write Logtalk source and it is compiled down to code for an existing Prolog system, which serves as the backend. The distribution also bundles libraries, developer tools, a handbook, API docs, and examples. The brew caveats show that the install is configured through the LOGTALKHOME and LOGTALKUSER environment variables. The executables it ships include per-backend launchers such as swilgt, gplgt, and yaplgt, plus lgt2html, lgt2md, lgt2pdf and similar documentation generators, and logtalk_tester.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to bring Prolog up to 'programming in the large' by adding code encapsulation and code reuse mechanisms while preserving Prolog's declarative features. The homepage pitches it as 'Logic Programming meets Software Engineering'.
brief.how_it_works: Logtalk source is compiled by a transcompiler into code for a standards-compliant Prolog system, which the README says can be most modern ones. It uses standard Prolog syntax plus some added operators and directives to ease the learning path. Multi-threading is available on selected backends only.

commands_seen.context: Mentioned in the README as a way to generate a list of the POSIX man pages for Logtalk's shell scripts. It appears in prose, not as a code block.

brief.install_notes: Install from sources by running a couple of shell scripts, or use an OS-specific installer from logtalk.org/download.html. Manual steps are in INSTALL.md, quick-start instructions are in QUICK_START.md, and customization is in CUSTOMIZE.md. You need a supported Prolog compiler installed first. Upgrading from Logtalk 2.x requires reading UPGRADING.md. Registration at logtalk.org/regform.html is optional. Homebrew sets LOGTALKHOME=$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/logtalk and LOGTALKUSER=$HOME/logtalk.
brief.standout: It is a layer over existing Prolog systems rather than a new Prolog, so you keep your backend and gain objects, protocols, and categories on top. The tool suite is unusually large for a niche language and is portable across backends.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage shows v3.102.0 dated September 14, 2026. The GitHub README carries a 1998-2026 copyright notice and links to active release notes, a discussions forum, and a Gitter chat.
brief.caveats: Requires a separately installed Prolog backend, and some features such as high-level multi-threading work only on selected backends. Going from Logtalk 2.x to 3.x needs manual porting per UPGRADING.md. The language is niche, so community size is small compared with mainstream languages. The fetched README did not show any build warnings.
quotes: Logtalk is a declarative object-oriented logic programming language that extends and leverages the Prolog language with a feature set suitable for programming in the large.

Distributed under a commercial-friendly license, it includes full documentation, extensive portable libraries, a comprehensive set of portable developer tools, and a large number of programming examples to help get you started.

judge.reason: Logtalk makes Prolog’s logic programming meet objects, protocols, and reusable components—a distinctive language to explore, with active maintenance and substantial documentation.

entry.title: Logtalk
entry.tldr: Logtalk adds objects, protocols, and hot-patchable components to Prolog by compiling down to the Prolog system you already have.
entry.deeper_look:
Logtalk is a declarative object-oriented logic programming language. It extends Prolog with prototypes, classes, protocols (interfaces), and categories, which are components that can be used to patch objects at runtime. It uses standard Prolog syntax plus a few added operators and directives, so the learning path is short if you already know Prolog.

It works as a transcompiler. You write Logtalk source, and it is compiled into code for a standards-compliant Prolog system, which the README says can be most modern ones. The Homebrew install ships a launcher for each supported backend, such as `swilgt`, `gplgt`, and `yaplgt`. The formula depends on GNU Prolog, so `gplgt` should work out of the box.

The README frames the goal as bringing Prolog up to 'programming in the large': code encapsulation and reuse, while keeping Prolog's declarative features. The homepage puts it as 'Logic Programming meets Software Engineering'. The idea underneath is that a logic language can have the structuring tools of mainstream OO languages without giving up its own way of computing.

The distribution also bundles libraries, a handbook, API docs, and many examples. There are developer tools too, including documentation generators (`lgt2html`, `lgt2md`, `lgt2pdf`, and others) and a test runner, `logtalk_tester`.
entry.install:
brew install logtalk
# Homebrew sets LOGTALKHOME=$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/logtalk and LOGTALKUSER=$HOME/logtalk
# Needs a Prolog backend; the formula pulls in gnu-prolog (use gplgt). Others, such as SWI-Prolog, are installed separately.

try_this.what_happens: Shows the options for the GNU Prolog launcher, which starts Logtalk on the backend Homebrew installs for you.
Shows the options for the SWI-Prolog launcher, if you have installed SWI-Prolog as a backend.
Lists the man pages for Logtalk's shell scripts, which is a quick way to see what the toolchain includes.

entry.whats_unique: It is a layer over existing Prolog systems rather than a new Prolog, so you keep your backend and gain objects, protocols, and categories on top. The tool suite is unusually large for a niche language and works across backends.
entry.caveats: It needs a Prolog backend, some features like high-level multi-threading work only on selected backends, and the community is small next to mainstream languages.
